author.name: John Scully
author.headline: Decentralized Medical Records System. Blockchain-based system, US patent 12266430

comments.text:
Thank you, Josh, for sharing your perspective. I believe the fundamental issue with the electronic health record (EHR) framework lies in its original design, which prioritized billing. The HITECH Act, implemented by President Obama with Judy Faulkner from Epic, marked a significant turning point for the concept of every patient having a single medical record. President Trump perceptively identified the core problem and stated, “We will put you in control of your own medical records. We require doctors to make your records available electronically, and you own them. You control them; they will be portable, allowing you to work seamlessly with all of your medical providers, which will make your life much easier.”

Achieving this goal is feasible by utilizing blockchain technology and adhering to the President's policy.

author.headline: Find Melanoma Answers @ BestIsMe.Org | Author - Missing Context Newsletter | Applied Research. Better Outcomes.

comments.text:
Interesting from an adoption angle because the technical standard is only half the battle.

If this can make health data sharing feel normal across web, mobile, Android, iOS wallets, FHIR resources, and patient check-in workflows, the next question is not just “does it work?” It is: will practices know how to use it, will patients understand why it matters, and will the workflow be simple enough that staff actually adopt it?

That is where a lot of digital health breaks down. The protocol can be solid, but if education, trust, front desk workflow, patient language, and implementation strategy are not solved, adoption stalls.

This is exactly the kind of topic we’re discussing in Digital Health Adoption Network: how to move good healthcare technology from standards and pilots into real practices, real patients, and real public use. Feel free to join and post the article there.

author.headline: Senior Project Manager | Healthcare Interoperability | FHIR | AI | Digital Health Innovation

comments.text:
This is a massive step toward true Patient Empowerment💪
​From my perspective, the real revolution happens when we combine this kind of seamless technology with AI Literacy for patients.
​Moving Verifiable Credentials directly into the browser (W3C API) removes the 'app fatigue' and puts the patient back in the driver's seat. But more importantly, it creates a foundation where patients can securely feed their own data into AI-driven decision support tools.
​When the UX is as simple as a digital wallet, we bridge the gap between complex health standards and real-world health literacy. It’s not just about 'data in the patient's hand' , it’s about giving them the tools and the knowledge to actually use it.
​Thanks for the update, Josh!🙏
